title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is bookkeeping inside Grothendieck's combinatorial model for the Galois/Teichmüller tower. The setup comes from pp. 53–54. There is a 'standard' group Π_{0,3}, the fundamental group of U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}. Its extension Π̃_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z) is generated by ρ, an order-3 symmetry permuting 0→1→∞, and the involutions σ_∞, σ̃_∞. Facing it is a 'concrete' copy Π_ε attached to an elementary piece of a decomposed surface: a pair of pants or 3-punctured sphere Σ* with three boundary points/cusps I, orientation data ω, and a 'side' ϖ. The previous page says a pinning (épinglage) of the situation is an element r = (i, ω, ϖ) ∈ Rep(I, ϖ) ≅ I × ω × ϖ, which determines ε = ω∧ϖ. It also introduces two pinning isomorphisms ψ_ε^{i,ω}: Π_{0,3} → Π_ε and ψ_i^{ω,ε}: Π_{0,3} → Π_i, linked by a commutative triangle with the comparison isomorphisms φ_{iε}, φ_{εi} (35).

This page first notes that, because of the triangle, it is enough to define one of the two isomorphisms. Given how Π_{0,3} was defined in (32), the natural one to define is Ψ_r: Π_{0,3} → Π_ε. It is defined by transport of structure. Ψ_r = π_1(u_r), where u_r: (U_{0,3}, P^+) → (Σ*, P_ω) is the unique conformal (biholomorphic) isomorphism carrying the standard frame {∞, 0, +1} to the frame (i, ω, ε). The base points are not points but simply connected regions: P^+ is the upper half-plane and P_ω the corresponding 'half' of Σ* fixed by the orientation/side data. So π_1 is canonically defined without choosing a path, and a conformal map respecting these regions induces a well-defined group isomorphism, not just one up to inner automorphism.

The marginal note spells out the dictionary. To (i, ω) one attaches the frame r = (ω_i, ω'_i; i) in 'usual terms', i.e. 0 ↦ ω_i, 1 ↦ ω'_i, ∞ ↦ i. Changing (i, ω) by the symmetry ρ composes the frame with ρ (roughly ρ(r) = r∘ρ). This makes the S_3-equivariance explicit.

The counting paragraph then says the following.
- For a fixed piece there are six frames, i.e. six choices of Ψ_r (the six orderings of the three cusps, an S_3-torsor).
- For fixed i there are four choices of (ω, ε): two orientations times two half-planes.
- If one has already fixed the real structure / side ϖ in Σ (so ε is determined by ω), one is down to three frames (the cyclic ones).
- One therefore needs a convenient way of passing from one choice to another, i.e. explicit formulas for the change-of-frame automorphisms of Π_{0,3}.

The next page carries this out. It shows Ψ_{g(r)} = π_1(g)∘Ψ_r for g in the stabiliser of ε, which acts simply transitively on frames over a fixed ε, and asks for explicit formulas in Π_{0,3} (ρ, σ_∞, τ_∞ from (33)). The purpose is to give rigid, Galois-compatible identifications of every 'pants' fundamental group with the standard π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}). This is the prerequisite for writing the Galois/GT action on the whole Teichmüller tower via gluing of elementary pieces, as in the Lego of the Esquisse.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The count 'four choices for ω, ε' for fixed i, and the reduction to three once the side is fixed, is consistent with 6 = |S_3| frames per piece and 12 = 3 × 2 × 2 total pinnings (I × ω × ϖ). The notation is unstable, though: the same isomorphism is written Ψ^{i,ω}_{ω,ε}, Ψ^{i,ω}_{ε,ε} and Ψ^{i,ω}_{ε,ϖ} within a few lines. The frame is first written {∞,0,+1} and then mapped to (i, ω, ε), so the exact matching of standard points to data is not fully fixed on this page (the margin gives 0↦ω_i, 1↦ω'_i, ∞↦i).

ideas.what: Using a simply connected region (upper half-plane P^+, half-surface P_ω) as base point, so that conformal maps induce genuine isomorphisms of π_1 rather than outer classes
ideas.modern_name: base points as simply connected domains; tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'), and Ihara for tangential base points; Grothendieck's half-plane base points are discussed around the Esquisse and in Drinfeld/Ihara-era GT literature
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) mentions base points along real/tangential data in the Teichmüller-tower discussion; not in this explicit form

ideas.what: Pinning isomorphisms Ψ_r: π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) ≅ π_1 of a 3-punctured piece, indexed by frames r (ordering of cusps plus orientation/side), with S_3 (extended by complex conjugation) acting simply transitively
ideas.modern_name: rigidification of pants groups by ordered marked points; S_3 × Z/2 symmetry of M_{0,4}/P^1−{0,1,∞}
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; implicit in Drinfeld's GT (1990) and Ihara's work, and in Lego/Teichmüller tower constructions (Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps)
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in Esquisse d'un programme §2 (Teichmüller tower, Lego); not with these formulas

ideas.what: Need for explicit change-of-frame formulas in Π_{0,3} (in terms of ρ, σ_∞, τ_∞ inside Π̃_{0,3} ≅ SL(2,Z))
ideas.modern_name: action of the automorphism group S_3 of P^1−{0,1,∞} on π_1 (Ihara's/Drinfeld's θ and ω relations)

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but routine bookkeeping: rigidifying pants fundamental groups via conformal maps and half-plane base points, and counting the 6/4/3 frame choices. The ideas (half-plane/tangential base points, the S_3-equivariance of P^1−{0,1,∞}) are well known in the GT/Teichmüller-tower literature. Nothing here goes beyond what Grothendieck sketched and later authors formalised.
transcription_corrections: Opening lines read: 'ce qui fait qu'il suffit de définir l'une des deux isom. (34) — et en vertu de la définition des Π_{0,3} dans (32), il est naturel de définir plutôt l'iso'.
Left label: 'r=(i;ω,ε_ω^ϖ)' with ε written over ϖ and ω, i.e. r = (i; ω, ϖ) with ε = ω∧ϖ; Ψ_r = Ψ^{i,ω}_{ϖ,ε}.

Display: 'Ψ^{i,ω}_{ε,ϖ} = [crossed out] π_1(u_{i,ω,ε,ϖ}, P^+), où u_r = u^{i,ω}_{ε,ϖ} : (U_{0,3}, P^+) → (Σ*, P_ω) est l'unique iso conforme qui transforme le repère standard {∞, 0, +1} dans le repère (i, ω, ε)'. The ':.' is 'où'.
Margin: 'Au couple (i,ω) on associe le repère (en termes habituels) r=(ω_i, ω'_i; i) de (35) [?], i.e. 0↦ω_i, 1↦ω'_i, ∞↦i — Variation avec (i,ω) : si r=r_{(i,ω)}, ρ(r)=r∘ρ [?]'.
'Pour un Pi fixé' is probably 'Pour un ε fixé' (or ϖ), and 'Qi fixé' is probably 'i fixé'.

Parenthetical is more likely '(ce qui fait trois rep. [replacing 'deux'] choix si on suppose qu'on a choisi une orientation de ϖ ou Σ en réalité dans ε = ω, et si on se borne aux ε qui correspondent à ω)'.
Last line is likely 'il faut donc un choix commode pour passer de l'un à l'autre', not 'communément privilégié'.
